easy.title: Top Customers by Orders
easy.question: Given a table orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date), return top 5 customers by total order count.
easy.hint: Use GROUP BY customer_id and ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC.
easy.solution: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY total_orders DESC LIMIT 5;

easy.title: Daily Active Users
easy.question: From events(user_id, event_time), find daily active users for the last 7 days.
easy.solution: SELECT DATE(event_time) AS day, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS dau FROM events WHERE event_time >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 day' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day;

medium.title: Month-over-Month Revenue
medium.question: Using sales(order_date, amount), compute month-over-month growth percentage.
medium.hint: Aggregate by month and use LAG() window function.
medium.solution: WITH m AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY 1) SELECT month, revenue, ROUND((revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month)) * 100.0 / NULLIF(LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0), 2) AS mom_growth_pct FROM m ORDER BY month;

medium.title: Find Duplicate Transactions
medium.question: Identify duplicate rows in transactions(txn_id, user_id, amount, created_at) where user_id, amount, and date match.
medium.hint: Use ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by natural key columns.
medium.solution: WITH ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, amount, DATE(created_at) ORDER BY created_at) AS rn FROM transactions) SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rn > 1;

hard.title: Sessionization
hard.question: From clickstream(user_id, event_time), create sessions where a new session starts after 30 minutes of inactivity.
hard.hint: Compare current event_time with LAG(event_time), then cumulative sum of new-session flags.
hard.solution: WITH ordered AS (SELECT user_id, event_time, CASE WHEN event_time - LAG(event_time) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_time) > INTERVAL '30 min' OR LAG(event_time) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_time) IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_new FROM clickstream), sessions AS (SELECT user_id, event_time, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_time) AS session_id FROM ordered) SELECT * FROM sessions;

hard.title: Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2
hard.question: Load customer_dim SCD2 from staging_customers capturing address changes with effective dates.
hard.hint: Close previous active record and insert new active version.
hard.solution: Use MERGE in two phases: (1) update active records setting end_date and is_current = false where tracked attributes changed; (2) insert new records with start_date = CURRENT_DATE, end_date = '9999-12-31', is_current = true.
